summary: @servicetitan/hash-browser-router ships install-time Bun-runtime dropper executing obfuscated payload
details: package.json declares scripts.preinstall = 'node setup.mjs', which runs automatically on npm install. setup.mjs is identifier-obfuscated (_0xXXXX names, helper-object dispatch, hand-rolled ZIP central-directory parser, musl detection via ldd --version and /etc/os-release parsing) and selects a platform/arch-specific Bun release from github.com/oven-sh/bun/releases/download/bun-v1.3.13/<target>.zip, downloads it over HTTPS, extracts the bun binary to a temp directory, chmod +x's it, and then executes a bundled sibling file math_init.js under that Bun binary (falling back to a system 'bun' if present). math_init.js is a ~727KB '// @bun @bun-cjs' blob obfuscated with a rotating string/int array (n7gIxM) plus a WV8StW rotator and hc1jfK9 alphabet-permutation decoder — the canonical string-array + shuffle + charcode decoder shape. A React hash-router library has no functional need to download an alternate JavaScript runtime at install time in order to execute a 700KB obfuscated sibling file with a misleading 'math_init.js' name; Node is already running the preinstall. The alternate-runtime dispatch is an evasion pattern that hides the executed code from scanners that only trace Node-resolved imports.
